Metrics / reporting / data quality

Turn business data into decisions your team can explain.

Define useful measures, prepare reliable data, and build dashboards and analysis views around real business questions. We connect the definition behind each number to the next decision and its owner.

Shape this service ↗Open the capability explorer →
Level 2Choose a capability

The constraint we solve.

Disconnected systems create conflicting totals and dashboards with unclear meaning. Reliable decision reporting requires shared definitions, reconciled data, appropriate comparison periods, and an understanding of what each measure can and cannot tell you.

Questions we begin with

  • What decision will a measure or dashboard help someone make?
  • Can the source records support the required formula and comparison consistently?
  • Who owns a changed definition, late source, or data-quality exception?

Who it can support

  • Leadership teams seeking a coherent view of commercial and operational performance.
  • Growth and product teams investigating funnel conversion, activation, and retention.
  • Organizations preparing consistent data for reporting and automation.

Executive dashboards and decision reporting

Level 4Inspect the detail

Give leadership a coherent view of the business questions that matter. We define measures, reconcile source data, and build decision views with clear periods, units, filters, and ownership.

Where it is useful

Funnel, cohort, and customer analysis

Level 4Inspect the detail

Understand where a journey loses momentum and which customer groups behave differently. We use matched definitions and time windows to turn funnel and cohort evidence into focused questions and experiments.

Where it is useful

  • Compare enquiry quality and conversion across campaigns using a consistent lead definition.
  • Identify friction between signup, the first useful product action, and repeat use.
  • Review retention by onboarding cohort, customer segment, or acquisition source.
  • A funnel and cohort specification with events, identities, eligible populations, and time windows.
  • An analysis view of stage conversion, activation, retention, and relevant segment differences.
  • A prioritized findings brief that distinguishes observed patterns, limitations, and next tests.
01

Define comparable groups

Agree the eligible population, events, customer identity, and observation windows. Separate immature cohorts and inconsistent tracking from useful comparisons.

Data foundations and quality operations

Level 4Inspect the detail

Make reporting and automation depend on reliable records. We design the identifiers, transformations, validation checks, and ownership needed to keep approved data usable as systems change.

Where it is useful

  • Prepare campaign and CRM data for a consistent commercial dashboard.
  • Reduce duplicate and incomplete records that cause operational handoff errors.
  • Introduce repeatable quality checks before datasets are used in automation or analysis.
  • A source inventory and data model documenting keys, field meaning, refresh rules, and ownership.
  • A selected ingestion and transformation workflow with validation, exception tracking, and version control.
  • A data-quality scorecard and recovery runbook for monitoring, investigation, and planned changes.
01

Map the source records

Document keys, fields, source ownership, and refresh expectations. Find where missing values, duplicates, and inconsistent definitions affect the business process.

Before implementation

  • The decisions and audience for the work, approved source access, and named metric owners.
  • Sample records and reconciliation evidence, reporting currencies, time zones, and refresh needs.
  • Agreement on definitions, comparison windows, permissions, and ongoing data ownership.
Can we begin with one focused capability?

Yes. Discovery identifies a useful scope with clear inputs, deliverables, owners, and acceptance checks. A broader engagement can connect additional capabilities once the first workflow and its dependencies are understood.

Will you work with our existing tools?

We review the existing stack before selecting or replacing a platform. Connections depend on the provider APIs, account plans, permissions, licensing, data quality, and the project scope; they are validated before being promised as part of delivery.

How do human expertise and AI work together?

Specialists own strategy, design, architecture, approved communication, and final business decisions. AI can assist bounded preparation and repeated tasks. Generated work is evaluated against representative examples and reviewed at the agreed points; uncertain cases have a named owner.
